newsitem.title: UK: CASH, DATED BRENT SEEN FIRMER BUT COULD RETRACE.
newsitem.headline: CASH, DATED BRENT SEEN FIRMER BUT COULD RETRACE.

text.p: Cash and Dated Brent firmed early on Tuesday amid light short-covering after recent hefty losses but traders said the grade could fall as quickly as it rose.

An August 23-25 cargo was reported to have fetched Sept Brent -15 cents a barrel to a U.S. major, five cents firmer than the last deal on Thursday, but other cargoes were still on offer at lower numbers.
"There's a bit of short-covering going on but I don't think Dated will stay up here for very long," said a trader.
Potential Brent sellers said earlier cargoes offered at around -20 cents were drawing bids no better than -27 cents.

Sept Brent on the IPE gained seven cents to $18.65 a barrel by 1200 GMT and intermonth cash spreads were also firmer, Sept/Oct trading at -13 cents and then -11 cents after three deals at -15 cents in late U.S. activity.
Short-dated Brent CFDs bounced higher on news of the firmer wet trade, next week's Aug 18-22 period seen bid at Oct Brent -30 cents, up about five cents from late Monday levels.
The only reported trade was an Aug 18-22/Sept 15-19 roll at -5 cents, dealers said.
Two Brent cargoes were due to be nominated Aug 27-29 loading dates on Tuesday, including Repsol's clocked Aug 26-28 which was deferred.
Other North Sea crudes were quiet and differentials broadly steady after recent hefty losses although some traders said they could have further to fall.
A Troll cargo loading Aug 30-Sep 1 was sold by a major to an NWE oil company for Dated Brent +21 cents.
In the Mediterranean, traders were waiting for confirmation that loading of Iraqi crude at the Turkish port of Ceyhan has begun.
